metadata.title: Height averages of Kloosterman sums and modular inverses

conventions.proof: A mathematical statement, identity, estimate, or calculation used in the written proof.
conventions.method: Reuse of a proof method, distinct from using the numerical assertion of that result.
conventions.literature: A cited external input at the precise locator recorded in the inventory.
conventions.source_locators: One-based line numbers in the identified v17 source. PDF pages are from its compiled auxiliary file.
conventions.synthetic_ids: The prefixes step:, geom:, support:, external:, and ov: are repository identifiers, not new manuscript labels or theorem numbers.
conventions.scope: Numbered statements and substantive supporting steps. Routine definitions and ambient arithmetic, calculus, measure theory and finite-sum manipulations are described where used, not represented as a formal axiomatic foundation.

nodes.title: Height-averaged cumulative second moment
nodes.summary: For real $N,X\ge1$, the height average of the second moment over $N\le\lvert n\rvert<2N$ is $\ll_\varepsilon (NX)^\varepsilon NX^2$. Both frequency signs are included.
notes: The actual proof invokes Lemma 3.2 directly, not the statement of Theorem 1.2. Theorem 1.2 is an equivalent presentation of the annular bound, but it is not the direct citation in this proof.

nodes.title: Height mean for moving intervals of moduli
nodes.summary: For $N,X\ge1$ and $0<\delta\le1$, restricting the moduli to $(Y,(1+\delta)Y]$ gives the height-mean bound $\ll_\varepsilon (NX)^\varepsilon X^2\{N\delta+\min(1,N\delta^2X)\}$.
notes: Do not create an edge from Theorem 1.2 to Lemma 3.2 merely because the introduction announces the theorem before its proof.

nodes.title: Exceptional heights for all real frequency cutoffs
nodes.summary: For $a,\kappa,\eta>0$ and $X\ge2$, outside a set of Lebesgue measure $O_{a,\kappa,\eta}(X^{1-\kappa+\eta})$, the bound $\mathcal K_2(N;Y)\le3NX^{2+\kappa}$ holds simultaneously for every real $1\le N\le X^a$.

nodes.title: Height-averaged discrepancy of pair differences
nodes.summary: For $X\ge2$, the height average of $\mathcal D_Y+\mathcal D_Y^*$ is $\ll_\varepsilon X^{-2+\varepsilon}$. Each discrepancy is at least $\lfloor Y\rfloor^{-2}$ for every $Y\ge2$. The supremum over rectangles is inside the average.
notes: Only the upper estimate is spectral via Proposition 3.4. The pointwise lower bound is elementary.

nodes.title: Exceptional heights for pair discrepancy
nodes.summary: For $\kappa,\eta>0$ and $X\ge2$, both discrepancies are at most $X^{-2+\kappa}$ outside a set of Lebesgue measure $O_{\kappa,\eta}(X^{1-\kappa+\eta})$.

nodes.title: Distance moments and covering radius
nodes.summary: For $X\ge2$, the positive distance moments have orders $X^{-s}$ for $0<s<2$, $X^{-2}(\log X)^2$ for $s=2$, and $X^{-1-s/2}$ for $s>2$. The covering radius lies between $\tfrac12X^{-1/2}$ and $4X^{-1/2}$.

nodes.title: Exact weighted Farey correction and its asymptotic
nodes.summary: For integer $Q\ge2$, $1/2\le\tau<1$ and $L=\tau Q^2$, an exact sinc-squared weighted second moment isolates determinant-one Farey pairs. Its asymptotic is $LN_Q+(12\tau/\pi^2)I(\tau)Q^4+O(Q^3\log(2Q))$, uniformly in $\tau$, with $I(\tau)>0$.
notes: The uniform Riemann-sum estimate is proved inside this theorem's proof.
Neither Proposition 6.1 nor Lemma 2.8 is an input.

nodes.title: Sharpness of the long-interval remainder
nodes.summary: For every sufficiently large integer $Q$, some symmetric interval with radius $T\asymp Q^2$ has a second-moment remainder whose absolute value is $\gg Q^4$. The constants are absolute; this is an existence statement for the interval.
notes: This is an absolute-value lower bound for the sharp interval remainder; it does not assert positivity of that sharp remainder.
The sharp cardinality asymptotic N_Q~(3/pi^2)Q^2 is not needed in the proof.

nodes.title: Kuznetsov formula and local spectral large sieve
nodes.summary: Records the inverse Kuznetsov formula for both signs and the local spectral large sieve on a window of width $G$, for $N,T\ge1$ and $1\le G\le T$. The formula uses the signed measure $dm=\chi\,dm_0$; the large sieve uses positive $dm_0$.
notes: Part (i) has the signed spectral measure; part (ii) has the positive spectral measure. These are two parts of one numbered lemma.

nodes.title: Dual spectral-window second moment
nodes.summary: Deduces a dual second-moment estimate $\ll_\eta F^2TG(TG+N)^{1+\eta}$ for a spectral-window integral with a multiplier bounded by $F$, for either sign.

references.role: source of the statement, not an additional input after the local derivation

nodes.title: Twisted transforms away from the low spectrum
nodes.summary: Records the uniform-in-$r$ twisted Bessel estimates in the imaginary range $\lvert t\rvert\ge1$ and the holomorphic range $k\ge1$. The low imaginary spectrum is treated separately in Lemma 2.4.
notes: This is Lemma 2.3, not the low-spectrum bound. The imaginary-parameter part is only asserted here for |t|>=1.

nodes.title: Low-spectrum transform estimate
nodes.summary: For $\lvert t\rvert\le1$ and $Z>0$, both twisted transforms are $\ll_V1+\log^+(1/Z)$, uniformly in the real twist $r$.
notes: Independent of the high-spectrum estimate in Lemma 2.3; do not draw a dependency 2.3 -> 2.4.

nodes.title: Weil bound for Kloosterman sums
nodes.summary: For all integer $m,n$ and $c\ge1$, $\lvert S(m,n;c)\rvert\le(m,n,c)^{1/2}c^{1/2}\tau(c)$.

nodes.title: Selberg's identity
nodes.summary: Expresses $S(m,n;c)$, for integer arguments, as a divisor sum of Kloosterman sums with one argument equal to one. The cumulative form is equation (2.6).

references.role: cited elementary proof for all integer arguments
historical announcement; no numbered locator supplied
historical first published proof; no numbered locator supplied at this citation

notes: The sum over divisors is positive divisors of the gcd. The all-zero frequency is not used in the later two-frequency mean.

nodes.title: Consecutive Farey fractions
nodes.summary: Consecutive fractions of Farey order $Q\ge1$ have determinant one and denominators whose sum exceeds $Q$.
notes: The adjacent-gap bounds are derived from this lemma. Nesting and the circular separation estimate recorded nearby have their own elementary arguments and are not applications of this lemma.

nodes.title: Two-sided large-sieve remainder
nodes.summary: For frequencies separated by $\lambda$ modulo one and any integer interval of length $H\ge1$, the absolute error from $H\sum_j\lvert y_j\rvert^2$ is at most $\lambda^{-1}\sum_j\lvert y_j\rvert^2$.

references.role: cosecant/Hilbert inequality bounding each endpoint sum

notes: No Farey lemma is needed for this abstract inequality. Farey separation is used only when it is applied later to the manuscript's specific frequencies.

nodes.title: Koksma-Szusz inequality with repetitions and general arcs
nodes.summary: Bounds rectangular discrepancy of a nonempty finite sequence in $\mathbb T^2$ by a Fourier sum and a truncation term, allowing repeated points and closed or half-open arcs, including empty and full arcs.
nodes.origin: Extension of a cited inequality, proved in v17

references.role: base inequality for distinct points and closed proper arcs

nodes.title: Twisted second moment
nodes.summary: For a fixed smooth compactly supported $W$, $C,N\ge1$ and real $r$, the second moment of the twisted smooth sums $B_\sigma(n,r)$ is $\ll_{\varepsilon,W}(NC(1+\lvert r\rvert))^\varepsilon(N+1+\lvert r\rvert)$.

references.role: method attribution: the source argument is followed with r retained; the actual inputs are Lemmas 2.1-2.4

nodes.title: Height mean for moving annuli of moduli
nodes.summary: Proves the moving-interval height mean at a base height $C\ge1$, with the factor $N\delta+\min(1,N\delta^2C)$. Theorem 1.2 is the corresponding formulation with signed frequencies.

references.role: divisor small-power bound invoked from the preliminary paragraph

notes: The delta C<1 case is elementary. The spectral/smoothing argument is used only for delta C>=1.

nodes.title: Weighted cumulative height mean
nodes.summary: For $N,X\ge1$, inserting the weight $1/c$ in the cumulative sums gives height-averaged second moment $\ll_\varepsilon(NX)^\varepsilon N$.

nodes.title: Height mean over a frequency rectangle
nodes.summary: For $M,N,X\ge1$, the height-averaged second moment over $\lvert m\rvert\le M$, $\lvert n\rvert\le N$, excluding $(0,0)$, is $\ll_\varepsilon(MNX)^\varepsilon MNX^2$. Both coordinate axes are included.

references.role: small-power divisor bounds, imported through the preliminary paragraph
Ramanujan-sum identity underlying the axis bound (2.7)

notes: In a graph that includes unnumbered facts, use Lemma 2.6 -> equation (2.6) -> Proposition 3.4. In a numbered-statements-only graph the direct collapsed predecessor is Lemma 2.6.

nodes.title: Weighted height mean over a frequency rectangle
nodes.summary: With the weight $1/c$, the same frequency rectangle has height-averaged second moment $\ll_\varepsilon(MNX)^\varepsilon MN$. The proof of Corollary 3.3 is reused with Proposition 3.4 as the input estimate.
nodes.origin: Proof transfer stated in the remark

nodes.title: Pointwise discrepancy of the difference measure
nodes.summary: For $Y\ge2$ and integer $K\ge1$, controls $\mathcal D_Y$ by weighted squared Fourier coefficients and $1/K$, and proves $\mathcal D_Y^*\le\mathcal D_Y+1/N_Y$.
notes: The Fourier coefficients of the difference multiset are |a_Y(k)|^2; repetitions and zero differences are retained in the first assertion.

nodes.title: A modular-inverse point in a product of Farey gaps
nodes.summary: If integers $Q,R\ge1$ satisfy $2QR\le X$, every product of open consecutive Farey gaps of orders $Q$ and $R$ contains a lift of a point of $\mathcal P_X$.
notes: Uses the determinant part of Lemma 2.7, not its denominator-sum part.

nodes.title: Adaptive Farey orders and their tail
nodes.summary: For $0<\rho\le1$ and irrational $x$, controls the least Farey order $R_\rho(x)$ giving a gap of length at most $\rho$. It proves the range $\rho^{-1/2}\le R_\rho(x)\le2/\rho$ and a quadratic tail estimate.
notes: R_rho is defined only on irrational coordinates; this suffices for the subsequent Lebesgue-measure arguments.

nodes.title: Tail of a product of adaptive Farey orders
nodes.summary: Bounds the tail of $\rho R_\rho(x)R_\rho(y)$ by a quadratic decay times the smaller of two logarithmic factors, for $1\le z\le4/\rho$; above this range the tail is empty on irrational-coordinate pairs.

nodes.title: Tail of the distance to modular-inverse points
nodes.summary: For $X\ge2$ and $t>0$, the measure of $\{d_X>t\}$ is $\ll [1+\min\{\log(2+Xt),\log(2+1/(Xt^2))\}]/(X^2t^2)$.

nodes.title: An arithmetic criterion for empty rectangles
nodes.summary: Gives an explicit arithmetic inequality in the denominators of the rational corner and the side lengths that makes two oppositely oriented open rectangles empty of lifts of $\mathcal P_X$.
notes: Independent of the preceding Farey-product/tail lemmas and of all spectral estimates.

nodes.title: Negative distance moments
nodes.summary: For $X\ge2$ and $-2<s<0$, the distance moment has order $X^{-s}$. For $s\le-2$ it diverges. The three assertions use disc counting, the positive first-moment upper bound, and a local singularity, respectively.
notes: Upper negative-moment bound: cardinality and disc-union area, not the positive first moment.
Lower negative-moment bound: Jensen and only the s=1 upper bound in Theorem 1.6; no use of its covering or lower-moment clauses.
Divergence at and below -2: local polar integral at the origin.
No statement for s=0 is made here.

nodes.title: Second moment over an arbitrary integer interval
nodes.summary: For integer $Q\ge2$, $M\in\mathbb Z$ and integer $H\ge1$, the second moment over $M<n\le M+H$ differs from $HN_Q$ by at most $Q(Q-1)N_Q$.
notes: The supporting equation (2.9) is defined in spectral_dependencies.json.
Montgomery-Vaughan enters through Lemma 2.8, not as an additional direct invocation.
Lemma 2.7 is not needed for the elementary separation argument.

nodes.title: Poisson identity for the sinc-squared weight
nodes.summary: For real $L\ge2$, the absolutely convergent Fourier series of $w(n/L)$ equals the triangular kernel $L(1-L\lVert\theta\rVert)_+$ for every real $\theta$.
notes: The weight w is defined in the introduction at lines 289-291 and recalled at line 1187.
The separate Plancherel theorem used in Section 3 is not an input here.

nodes.title: Exact contribution of determinant-one pairs
nodes.summary: For integer $Q\ge2$ and real $L\ge Q^2/2$, evaluates the weighted second moment as the diagonal term $LN_Q$ plus the contribution of determinant-one Farey pairs. The correction vanishes for $L\ge Q(Q-1)$.
notes: The determinant-one classification is proved directly; no theorem on ordinary Farey correlations is invoked.
The proof does not use Proposition 6.1 or the large sieve.

nodes.title: Positivity of the Farey correction integral
nodes.summary: For $1/2\le\tau<1$, reduces $I(\tau)$ to a one-dimensional integral and proves it is positive. On $[1/2,5/8]$ it gives the explicit lower bound $1/9000$.
notes: Equation (1.19) supplies a definition only; there is no proof edge from Theorem 1.7 to this lemma.

nodes.title: Low-spectrum Bessel kernel bounds
nodes.summary: Bounds the Schlaefli remainder integral and both low-spectrum kernels by $1+\log^+(1/x)$, then integrates over the fixed scaled support.

nodes.title: Kloosterman symmetries
nodes.summary: Records reality, interchange of the two arguments, and simultaneous sign reversal of Kloosterman sums. In particular, $S(-n,1;c)=S(n,-1;c)$.

nodes.title: Small-power divisor bound
nodes.summary: Uses $\tau(n)\ll_\eta n^\eta$ for every $\eta>0$.

nodes.title: Cumulative Selberg identity
nodes.summary: Sums Selberg's identity over the modulus to reduce $A_Y(m,n)$ to divisor-weighted sums $A_{Y/d}(mn/d^2,1)$ for $mn\ne0$. Terms with $d>Y$ vanish.

nodes.title: Ramanujan sums on the coordinate axes
nodes.summary: The Ramanujan-sum formula gives $\lvert A_Y(0,n)\rvert\le Y\tau(\lvert n\rvert)$ for $n\ne0$. Interchange of arguments covers the other axis.

nodes.title: Lengths of adjacent Farey gaps
nodes.summary: The length of an adjacent Farey gap is $1/(qq')$ and lies between $Q^{-2}$ and $Q^{-1}$.

nodes.title: Nesting of Farey intervals
nodes.summary: Increasing the Farey order adds fractions, so every new gap is contained in an old gap.
notes: Uses the definition of the Farey sequence, not Lemma 2.7.

nodes.title: Circular separation of reduced fractions
nodes.summary: Distinct reduced fractions modulo one, with denominators at most $Q\ge2$, are separated by at least $1/[Q(Q-1)]$. The proof uses denominator arithmetic directly.
notes: Proof is by denominator arithmetic, split into c!=d and c=d. It does not use adjacency and does not depend on Lemma 2.7.

nodes.title: Endpoint sums in the large-sieve remainder
nodes.summary: Writes the off-diagonal interval sum as a difference of two cosecant bilinear forms and bounds each by the Montgomery-Vaughan inequality.

nodes.title: Perturbation and arc approximation
nodes.summary: Perturbs repeated points to distinct points and passes to limits. Monotone approximation then covers the stated arc conventions and degeneracies.

nodes.title: Spectral decomposition of the twisted sums
nodes.summary: Applies Kuznetsov with a scalar of modulus one, separates low, holomorphic, and higher imaginary spectral ranges, and sums the window estimates by Minkowski.

nodes.title: Elementary moving-interval estimate
nodes.summary: Counts the moduli in a moving interval and the logarithmic height measure contributed by each modulus; the Weil and divisor bounds give the elementary mean-square estimate.

nodes.title: Mellin transform of the smoothed interval
nodes.summary: Constructs a smooth approximation to the moving interval and bounds its Mellin transform in terms of the interval length and the smoothing width.

nodes.title: Plancherel identity for the height average
nodes.summary: The substitution $Y=C\exp(u)$ converts the height mean of the smooth sums to a Fourier Plancherel integral in the twist parameter.
notes: This identity needs the definitions of the weights and B_sigma, not Lemma 3.1's estimate. Equation (1.24) in the introduction is the same identity announced earlier.

nodes.title: Smooth moving-interval height mean
nodes.summary: Combines the twisted second moment, Mellin decay, and Plancherel to bound the smoothed height mean.

nodes.title: Removal of smoothing and comparison of bounds
nodes.short_title:
Remove smoothing;
combine the two bounds
nodes.summary: The smoothing changes at most two boundary moduli on the relevant height block. Bounds this error by Weil, then combines the spectral and elementary estimates to obtain the minimum in Lemma 3.2.

nodes.title: Dyadic decomposition of the cumulative sum
nodes.summary: Decomposes the cumulative modulus sum into dyadic annuli and uses Minkowski. At most two contributing blocks lie below base height one; these are treated directly.

nodes.title: Exceptional set uniform over real cutoffs
nodes.summary: Applies Chebyshev on finitely many dyadic frequency blocks and covers each real interval $[N,2N)$ by two adjacent blocks. Their lengths sum to at most $3N$.

nodes.title: Vector partial summation for the weight 1/c
nodes.summary: Applies partial summation coordinatewise and Minkowski to a finite vector of frequencies. An unweighted height mean then supplies the corresponding mean with weight $1/c$.
notes: As a method node this is independent of a specific input estimate. Corollary 3.3 supplies Theorem 1.1 as that input; Remark 3.5 supplies Proposition 3.4 instead. Do not make the method node depend on Corollary 3.3's conclusion.

nodes.title: Divisor reduction and treatment of the axes
nodes.summary: Uses cumulative Selberg, Cauchy-Schwarz, and divisor counting to apply Theorem 1.1. Treats base heights below one directly and handles the coordinate axes separately.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of ordered differences
nodes.summary: The normalized Fourier coefficient of the multiset of ordered differences is the squared absolute value of the coefficient of the original point set.

nodes.title: Removal of diagonal pairs
nodes.summary: Splits the difference measure into distinct pairs and a mass $1/N_Y$ at zero. The resulting discrepancy change is at most $1/N_Y$.

nodes.title: Dyadic frequency blocks for discrepancy
nodes.summary: Uses Proposition 3.4 and the cardinality comparison to bound each weighted dyadic frequency block. The blocks on the axes are retained; the origin is excluded.
notes: The j=0 blocks include the coordinate axes; remove k=(0,0) before using Proposition 3.4.

nodes.title: Upper discrepancy bound
nodes.summary: Sums the frequency blocks, applies Lemma 4.1, and chooses the Fourier cutoff of order $X^2$ to prove the upper discrepancy bound.

nodes.title: Injectivity of the first coordinate
nodes.summary: The first coordinate determines the reduced denominator and then its unique modular inverse. Thus distinct points have distinct first coordinates, including the modulus-one origin.
notes: Uniqueness of reduced denominator and of the modular inverse; includes the modulus-one origin.

nodes.title: Lower discrepancy bound from an empty strip
nodes.summary: Circular separation gives a strip containing no differences, including no diagonal difference. Letting its left endpoint approach zero gives the lower discrepancy bound.
notes: No spectral input and no upper discrepancy estimate.

nodes.title: Upper covering bound from Farey products
nodes.summary: Takes $Q=\lfloor\sqrt{X/2}\rfloor$ and uses a point in every product of Farey gaps to obtain the upper covering bound, including rational endpoints by closure.
notes: Choose closed Farey intervals at rational endpoints; the constructed lift lies inside their open product.

nodes.title: Adaptive Farey intervals
nodes.summary: Combines the Farey gap bounds with nesting and defines the least order at which the gap containing an irrational coordinate is short enough.

nodes.title: Layer-cake identity for positive moments
nodes.summary: Expresses a positive distance moment as the integral of its tail by Tonelli's theorem.

nodes.title: Upper bounds for positive distance moments
nodes.summary: Integrates the distance-tail estimate in the three ranges of $s$, using the already proved upper covering bound for the support cutoff.
notes: The first logarithm is used for s<=2 and the second for s>2. The support cutoff comes from the already proved upper covering bound.

nodes.title: Counting lower bound for positive moments
nodes.summary: The union of small discs around the $N_X$ points covers at most half the torus. This gives a lower moment bound of order $X^{-s}$ for every fixed $s>0$.

nodes.title: Moment of the distance to a square boundary
nodes.summary: On an empty square, the distance to the point set is at least the distance to the boundary. Integrates this boundary distance explicitly.

nodes.title: Supercritical lower bound from one empty square
nodes.summary: One empty square of side $1/(2\sqrt X)$ gives the lower moment bound of order $X^{-1-s/2}$ for $s>2$.

nodes.title: Disjoint empty-square packing
nodes.summary: Packs disjoint empty squares near rational pairs with small denominators. Their contributions produce the square of a harmonic totient sum.
notes: This is the source of the two independent harmonic denominator sums.

nodes.title: Harmonic sum of totients
nodes.summary: Derives $\sum_{q\le y}\varphi(q)/q^2=(6/\pi^2)\log y+O(1)$ by the elementary Mobius formula and a harmonic-sum estimate.
notes: Derived in the manuscript; do not turn it into an uncited dependence on a specialized external theorem.

nodes.title: Critical second-moment lower bound
nodes.summary: Combines the disjoint-square packing with the totient sum to obtain the critical $X^{-2}(\log X)^2$ lower bound. The counting bound covers the remaining bounded range of heights.

nodes.title: Empty tangent disc and lower covering bound
nodes.summary: Proves directly that a disc tangent at the origin contains no lift of the point set. This gives the lower covering bound independently of the empty-rectangle lemma.
notes: This is independent of Lemma 5.5; do not connect the empty-rectangle criterion as a required predecessor.

nodes.title: Upper bound for negative moments
nodes.summary: Disc counting and the layer-cake identity for negative powers establish finiteness and the upper bound for $-2<s<0$.
notes: Proves finiteness before using Jensen; negative powers at the finitely many points of P_X are harmless measure-zero singularities.

nodes.title: Lower bound for negative moments
nodes.summary: Jensen's inequality and only the upper first-moment estimate in Theorem 1.6 give the lower bound for negative moments.
notes: The upper first-moment bound gives the lower negative-moment bound because s<0. Finiteness was already proved in geom:negative-upper, but extended Jensen also gives the lower inequality without using that estimate. Do not reverse the roles.

nodes.title: Divergence of negative moments
nodes.summary: The origin belongs to the point set, so a local polar integral proves divergence for $s\le-2$.
notes: No positive-moment or Farey estimate is needed.

nodes.title: Size of the modular-inverse point set
nodes.summary: The summatory totient estimate gives $N_X=(3/\pi^2)X^2+O(X\log(2X))$, hence $N_Y\asymp X^2$ for $X\le Y\le2X$. The discrepancy proof needs the lower bound for normalization.

nodes.title: Elementary upper bound for the cardinality
nodes.summary: The identity $N_X=\sum_{c\le X}\varphi(c)$ and $\varphi(c)\le c$ give $N_X\le X^2$ for $X\ge1$. This is sufficient for the distance counting arguments and the interval remainder bound.

nodes.title: Trigonometric-polynomial representation
nodes.summary: Opens the Kloosterman sums to express $A_Q(n,1)$ using the $N_Q$ distinct reduced fractions as frequencies and inverse phases of modulus one as coefficients.

nodes.title: Determinant-one pair calculation
nodes.summary: Compact support restricts the centered determinant residue to $+1$ or $-1$. The Chinese remainder theorem counts the pairs; their conjugate inverse phases give the cosine correction.

nodes.title: Uniform coprime lattice sum
nodes.summary: A uniform Lipschitz bound permits a Riemann-sum comparison on each sublattice. Mobius inversion produces the coprime main term and the $O(Q\log(2Q))$ error before multiplication by $2L$.
notes: The lattice estimate itself is proved locally. Lemma 6.3 connects this coprime sum with the weighted moment, at the level of Theorem 1.7.

nodes.title: Abel summation and variation localization
nodes.summary: Combines the uniform sharp-interval remainder bound with the positive weighted correction. Abel summation and small variation near zero and in the far tail force a large remainder at radius comparable to $Q^2$.

nodes.title: Kuznetsov formula and local spectral large sieve
nodes.summary: Kuznetsov formula and local spectral large sieve; BRS, Lemma 4.3.

nodes.title: Twisted Bessel transform estimates
nodes.summary: Twisted Bessel transform estimates; BRS, Lemma 4.2.

nodes.title: Koksma-Szusz base inequality
nodes.summary: Koksma-Szusz base inequality; BRS, Lemma 2.1.

nodes.title: Integral representations of J and K Bessel functions
nodes.summary: Integral representations of J and K Bessel functions; DLMF, Equations (10.9.6) and (10.32.9).

nodes.title: Weil bound
nodes.summary: Weil bound; IK, Corollary 11.12.

nodes.title: Divisor small-power bound
nodes.summary: Divisor small-power bound; IK, Equation (1.81).

nodes.title: Selberg identity for integer arguments
nodes.summary: Selberg identity for integer arguments; Xi, Equation (1.1).

nodes.title: Adjacent Farey fractions
nodes.summary: Adjacent Farey fractions; HW, Theorems 28 and 30.

nodes.title: Ramanujan-sum identity
nodes.summary: Ramanujan-sum identity; HW, Theorem 271.

nodes.title: Summatory totient asymptotic
nodes.summary: Summatory totient asymptotic; HW, Theorem 330.

nodes.title: Cosecant bilinear inequality and endpoint argument
nodes.summary: Cosecant bilinear inequality and endpoint argument; MV, Lemma 2, equation (2.1); proof of Theorem 1.

nodes.title: Plancherel theorem
nodes.summary: Plancherel theorem; Grafakos, Theorem 2.2.14 (4).

nodes.title: Poisson summation
nodes.summary: Poisson summation; Grafakos, Theorem 3.2.8.

discussion.title: Individual heights
discussion.summary: Open pointwise bounds remain distinct from the proved height averages and exceptional-set corollaries.

discussion.title: Small-power factors
discussion.summary: Discusses replacing epsilon losses by logarithmic factors; no stronger bound is asserted.

discussion.title: Distance constants
discussion.summary: The sharper covering constants follow from the Farey-product upper calculation and the independent tangent-disc lower calculation. Existence of limiting normalized moments or a limiting covering constant remains open.

discussion.title: Long ranges and a fixed second argument
discussion.summary: Discusses unevaluated higher determinants and the open question of an unweighted asymptotic at scale $Q^2$. The final paragraph adapts the Section 6 proofs to fixed nonzero integer $h$, choosing $\tau=1-1/(4\sqrt{\lvert h\rvert})$; its constants depend on $h$. This is an unnumbered extension, not an extra theorem.
